decisions.question: How should the plugin's Running it state the exit codes of a plugin that does not load, so that an app's CI does not read exit 0 as 'the rules ran'?

options.label: codes plus the one reliable outcome
options.consequence: A new paragraph states the analyzer's behavior (failure on stderr, exit by the other diagnostics, 4 when none) and that only exit 0 with no diagnostic reported, which every exit 0 under --fatal-infos is, shows the rules ran; every other outcome needs the stderr line. Describes SDK behavior in prose, no guarantee.

options.label: codes only
options.consequence: States the corrected codes and leaves the inference to the reader; shorter, but the step's purpose (nobody reads exit 0 as 'the rules ran') is left to the app's author.

options.label: a new guarantee with a recorded case
options.consequence: Makes the plugin-failure exit codes a contract promise; they are the Dart SDK's behavior, not nidana's, no producer phase can deliver them, and a recorded case would need a broken plugin under hsdd/contract/fixture/, which the replay of every other analyze case would then load.

decisions.chosen: codes plus the one reliable outcome
decisions.why: The app-shaped experiment shows that, when the plugin does not load, exit 1 to 3 come from the analyzer's own diagnostics, 4 from a run with nothing reported (a seeded rule violation included, A8), and 0 without --fatal-infos from INFOs alone (A4, A11); only exit 0 with nothing reported implies a loaded plugin (A1 versus A2, A3, A10). That inference is the useful sentence for app CI, and it rests on SDK behavior, so it stays prose that cites the experiment rather than a guarantee. The stderr text is named as the SDK's and not part of the contract, consistent with the contract's existing stance on stderr. The signal that would favor a guarantee: nidana shipping its own wrapper command whose exit code it controls.

The signal that would change this: In CI adding `generate` into build/.

experiments.question: What does `fvm dart analyze .` exit with, and where does it report the failure, when an app outside any workspace enables, by absolute path, an analysis server plugin that does not compile or does not resolve?
experiments.finding: The failure line goes to stderr in both output forms (A2 to A12). With the plugin not loading, the exit code follows the app's other diagnostics: ERROR 3 (A7), WARNING 2 (A6, A12), INFO 0 without --fatal-infos (A4, A11) and 1 with it (A5), and 4 when nothing is reported, with or without --fatal-infos (A2, A3, A9, A10), including an app whose only defect is a violation of the plugin's rule (A8). A loaded plugin on a clean app exits 0 (A1) and reports its rule (A0, A13). So exit 0 with no diagnostic reported, which every exit 0 under --fatal-infos is, implies the plugin loaded; no other outcome tells. Resolution failure (pub exit 69) and compile failure behave alike. Same pins as plugin-compile-exit/ (Dart 3.13.5 under Flutter 3.47.7, analyzer 13.3.0, analysis_server_plugin 0.3.18).
